text:
elena: quick sync — i'm attaching the PRD draft for the runtime dispatch change. goal: reduce P95 token latency by 15% for long-context inference while keeping unit-cost within 5% of current. need engineering scope + acceptance criteria by EOD tomorrow.

elena: high-level asks: 1) kernel selection policy (latency-first vs cost-first) with safe fallback, 2) attention micro-optimizations plan (compat with fp16/qq), 3) kv cache eviction semantics for multi-tenant GPUs.

sam: reading. can we bound rollout risk? what's the rollback plan if we see quality regressions? :thinking_face:

elena: rollback: auto-fallback to previous kernel variant per model-version + global toggle -> instant routing to stable pool. also manual canary: 5% traffic split.

marta: acceptance criteria suggestion:
- latency: P95 decrease >= 12% across our benchmark set
- cost: token cost change <= +5%
- quality: decoding perplexity within 1% relative to baseline on eval prompts
- safety: no increase in safety filter hits > 0.5%
put that as checklist?

nate: 👍 add observability: token-level timing, kernel-id tag, kv-hit/miss counts, per-model sample traces for cases where latency regresses.

jun: implementation note: kernel selection will require a per-request feature vector (seq_len, batch_size, model_arch, quant_mode). we'll need a tiny runtime decision table + metric to detect mispredictions.

elena: good — include config example in RFC. quick snippet: 
```
dispatch_policy:
  - when: seq_len >= 1024
    prefer: attn-optimized-kernel-v2
  - when: quant_mode == "4bit"
    prefer: quant-friendly-kernel
  - fallback: stable-kernel-v1
```

sam: edge case: mixed-batch requests (different seq_len) — do we force separate scheduling or use worst-case kernel? cost/latency tradeoff there. want explicit choice in spec.

marta: propose split strategy: separate by max-seq in batch if batch_size <= 4, otherwise isolate big-context requests to dedicated slot. documented in rollout gating.

infra-bot: automated test matrix queued: kernels x quant_modes x seq_ranges. job id: infra-8241.

nate: KV eviction edge-case: when cache eviction causes partial kv-miss mid-seq (prefetch race), we should detect and either re-run prefix prefetch or fall back to single-token replay. need to list acceptable user-visible latency overhead for that recovery path.

elena: add acceptance criterion: recovery overhead < 100ms p95 for <= 4096 context. add test harness to simulate eviction races.

jun: security/tenant isolation note: ensure kv caches are namespace-scoped. add KMS audit hook for any KV prefetch metadata if we surface customer ids in traces.

sam: ops ask: require canary metrics to include user-impacting error rates + tail latency buckets. + automatic pause if errors > 0.2% over 10m.

marta: will draft the RFC section for metrics and gating. elena, want me to propose a phased rollout timeline?

elena: yes — please. Phase 0: perf eval + unit tests. Phase 1: internal canary (10% infra), Phase 2: limited beta (select customers), Phase 3: full. include rollback triggers.

ci-bot: note: lint fails on PR #4021 (missing acceptance checklist).

nate: i'll own the recovery tests and observability hooks. sam/jun, can you pair on mixed-batch scheduling design?

sam: yep, i'll pair tomorrow morning.

jun: works for me.

elena: great — final asks: 1) RFC with config examples + gating checklist, 2) test matrix and harness for kv races, 3) rollout timeline and rollback triggers. tagging @sam @marta @nate for ownership. thanks! :raised_hands:
